summary: Milestone 3 Module 2 (Secure parent–teacher messaging) tested end-to-end on backend + frontend web preview (390x844). Backend pytest: tests/test_m3_messaging.py = 2/2 passed; full backend suite = 106 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing restart-persistence skip, unrelated). Parent flow (parent@sunrise.demo): Family home 'Messages' row (open-parent-messages) opened /messages; 'Message a teacher' (new-conversation-button) rendered the sheet with 2 child chips (conv-child-*) for a multi-child parent, 1 teacher button (conv-teacher-<id>) scoped to that child's section, conv-topic-input, conv-body-input. Submitting via new-conv-send POSTed /conversations and navigated to /messages/<id> with thread-list showing the message bubble; msg-input + msg-send sent a follow-up that appeared immediately (bubble count 3 -> 4). Teacher flow (teacher@sunrise.demo): Today 'Parent messages' row (teacher-messages-row) opened /messages list where conv-<id> card showed unread badge (conv-unread-<id> = 1). Opening the thread showed parent's two messages; sending via msg-input/msg-send bumped bubbles 4 -> 5. All three teacher actions (conv-follow-up, conv-escalate, conv-close) are visible and functional — follow-up tap flipped label to 'Clear follow-up', escalate tap moved conversation to escalated state (toast 'Updated'). Polling verified: parent reloading the thread screen (via navigate) sees 'Teacher reply to UI test' and the parent's own messages flip to 'Read' status (useInfiniteQuery refetchInterval 5000ms). Principal flow (principal@sunrise.demo): Command Centre 'Escalated messages' tile (quick-escalations) opened /messages escalated list showing the escalated conv-<id>; opening it rendered thread-list with all 5 messages. Principal does NOT see teacher-only actions (conv-follow-up/escalate/close hidden). Regression: principal quick-notices / quick-homework / quick-exams / quick-timetable all present (M3M1 + M2 unaffected). No deprecated expo packages (expo-av/expo-barcode-scanner/expo-background-fetch) found in repo. No red screen errors, no console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_messaging._access() re-checks live relationships on every request (parent_links membership, teacher assignment to the student's section, leader+escalated). This correctly handles revocation mid-session: a parent who loses guardianship or a teacher whose assignment is removed immediately gets 404 on the thread, which is stronger than role-only auth.

Idempotency: _post() short-circuits on (conversation_id, client_id) and additionally catches DuplicateKeyError, so network-retry storms with the same client_id never duplicate messages. The frontend reuses the same `pending` client id on error toast, satisfying the end-to-end contract.

Rate limit (20 per 10 min per sender_user_id) uses a time-windowed count_documents on the global messages collection — correct and tenant-safe because sender_user_id is unique per tenant. Verified by the pytest spam-loop asserting 429 appears.
Pydantic StartIn and MsgIn enforce body length (1..2000) and client_id length (8..64) — defends against empty or oversized payloads before sanitize().

sanitize() reused from routes_notices strips HTML tags, so the test's '' body is stored as plain text and surfaces with no '<' characters in the message list (verified in the pytest and reflected in the UI bubble which renders via ).

_conv_out() pops guardian_user_id/teacher_user_id for all sides and additionally pops follow_up for parents — the response payload never leaks the follow-up flag to parents (verified by assertion in test_parent_teacher_round_trip_...). It also never includes parent phone numbers (users doc isn't projected beyond name).

GET /messages marks only messages whose sender_role != viewer side as read and zeros that side's unread counter — avoids a leader (admin side) accidentally resetting counters, and never flips the parent's own 'mine' bubbles to read-by-self.

Attachment ACL (can_read_message_file) requires the file to be referenced by a message in a conversation the viewer still has _access() to; outsiders including the owner of a different tenant get 403 on /files/<id> (verified in pytest).

Teacher POST on a conversation where status=='closed' returns 400 with a clear message; parent POST on a closed conversation re-opens via the $set in _post — matches the 'parent reopens by replying' UX contract and is tested indirectly through the escalate/close/reopen suite.

set_status enforces act whitelist via Literal and gates parent-side acts to 'close' only; escalation and follow-up are teacher-side; the audit log emits one conversation.<act> event per transition (verified in test).

Frontend messages/index.tsx: Parent list action FAB is positioned absolutely; leaders see only the 'Escalated' Segmented. This prevents a leader from stumbling into a 'new conversation' sheet they aren't authorised to use.

Frontend messages/[id].tsx: useInfiniteQuery with refetchInterval=5000 polls the newest page every 5s (per spec); older pages lazy-load via onEndReached + next_cursor. The `pending` client-id state ensures the retry button reuses the same client_id so backend idempotency actually triggers.

Minor observation (not a bug, worth noting): the thread view renders msg-input and msg-send for ALL viewers including leaders (admin side). The backend _post() with side='admin' would create a message with sender_role='admin' (other='parent' is incremented); while access gating is correct, the UX contract for leaders is likely view-only. Consider hiding the compose dock when membership.role is in {owner, principal, school_admin}. The current test suite does not exercise an admin POST, so this doesn't break any test, but it would be a cleaner guard for the leaders UX.
No file exceeds the 700-line soft limit (routes_messaging.py=321, messages/index.tsx=97, messages/[id].tsx=105).
seed_data_creation: One MTEST conversation ('MTEST ui <epoch>') was created via the Parent UI, exchanged 5 messages across parent+teacher, and escalated. All data (1 conversation + 3 remaining messages after dedupe) was cleaned up via a direct Mongo delete on topic ~ '^MTEST'. The pytest helper _cleanup() in test_m3_messaging.py already purges its own fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login testIDs: login-email-input, login-password-input, login-submit-button. Parent path: open-parent-messages (family home) -> /messages -> new-conversation-button -> new-conv-sheet (conv-child-* chips if >1 child, conv-teacher-<id>, conv-topic-input, conv-body-input) -> new-conv-send -> /messages/<id> (thread-list, msg-<msgId>, msg-input, msg-send). Teacher path: teacher-messages-row -> /messages -> conv-<convId> / conv-unread-<convId> -> /messages/<id> + action bar (conv-follow-up, conv-escalate, conv-close). Principal path: quick-escalations -> /messages escalated list -> conv-<convId>. Rate limit is 20 msgs per sender per 10 min — don't spam msg-send in UI tests. Thread uses 5s polling + 15s list polling via @tanstack/react-query refetchInterval, no SSE/websocket. parent@sunrise.demo has 2 children (Aarav/Ishaan). Backend public URL is EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from frontend/.env.
